18.14: I tell you, this sinner, not the Pharisee, returned home justified before God. For those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.”
18.15: One day some parents brought their little children to Jesus so he could touch and bless them. But when the disciples saw this, they scolded the parents for bothering him.
18.16: Then Jesus called for the children and said to the disciples, “Let the children come to me. Don’t stop them! For the Kingdom of God belongs to those who are like these children.
18.17: I tell you the truth, anyone who doesn’t receive the Kingdom of God like a child will never enter it.”
18.18: Once a religious leader asked Jesus this question: “Good Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life?”
18.19: “Why do you call me good?” Jesus asked him. “Only God is truly good.
18.20: But to answer your question, you know the commandments: ‘You must not commit adultery. You must not murder. You must not steal. You must not testify falsely. Honor your father and mother.’”
18.21: The man replied, “I’ve obeyed all these commandments since I was young.”
18.22: When Jesus heard his answer, he said, “There is still one thing you haven’t done. Sell all your possessions and give the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me.”
18.23: But when the man heard this he became very sad, for he was very rich.
18.24: When Jesus saw this, he said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the Kingdom of God!
18.25: In fact, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the Kingdom of God!”
18.26: Those who heard this said, “Then who in the world can be saved?”
18.27: He replied, “What is impossible for people is possible with God.”
18.28: Peter said, “We’ve left our homes to follow you.”
18.29: “Yes,” Jesus replied, “and I assure you that everyone who has given up house or wife or brothers or parents or children, for the sake of the Kingdom of God,
18.30: will be repaid many times over in this life, and will have eternal life in the world to come.”
18.31: Taking the twelve disciples aside, Jesus said, “Listen, we’re going up to Jerusalem, where all the predictions of the prophets concerning the Son of Man will come true.
18.32: He will be handed over to the Romans, and he will be mocked, treated shamefully, and spit upon.
18.33: They will flog him with a whip and kill him, but on the third day he will rise again.”
18.34: But they didn’t understand any of this. The significance of his words was hidden from them, and they failed to grasp what he was talking about.
18.35: As Jesus approached Jericho, a blind beggar was sitting beside the road.
18.36: When he heard the noise of a crowd going past, he asked what was happening.
18.37: They told him that Jesus the Nazarene was going by.
18.38: So he began shouting, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
18.39: “Be quiet!” the people in front yelled at him. But he only shouted louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
18.40: When Jesus heard him, he stopped and ordered that the man be brought to him. As the man came near, Jesus asked him,
18.41: “What do you want me to do for you?” “Lord,” he said, “I want to see!”
18.42: And Jesus said, “All right, receive your sight! Your faith has healed you.”
18.43: Instantly the man could see, and he followed Jesus, praising God. And all who saw it praised God, too.

8.1: Soon afterward Jesus began a tour of the nearby towns and villages, preaching and announcing the Good News about the Kingdom of God. He took his twelve disciples with him,
8.2: along with some women who had been cured of evil spirits and diseases. Among them were Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons
8.3: Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod’s business manager; Susanna; and many others who were contributing from their own resources to support Jesus and his disciples.
8.4: One day Jesus told a story in the form of a parable to a large crowd that had gathered from many towns to hear him:
8.5: “A farmer went out to plant his seed. As he scattered it across his field, some seed fell on a footpath, where it was stepped on, and the birds ate it.
8.6: Other seed fell among rocks. It began to grow, but the plant soon wilted and died for lack of moisture.
8.7: Other seed fell among thorns that grew up with it and choked out the tender plants.
8.8: Still other seed fell on fertile soil. This seed grew and produced a crop that was a hundred times as much as had been planted!” When he had said this, he called out, “Anyone with ears to hear should listen and understand.”
8.9: His disciples asked him what this parable meant.
8.10: He replied, “You are permitted to understand the secrets of the Kingdom of God. But I use parables to teach the others so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled: ‘When they look, they won’t really see. When they hear, they won’t understand.’
8.11: “This is the meaning of the parable: The seed is God’s word.
8.12: The seeds that fell on the footpath represent those who hear the message, only to have the devil come and take it away from their hearts and prevent them from believing and being saved.
8.13: The seeds on the rocky soil represent those who hear the message and receive it with joy. But since they don’t have deep roots, they believe for a while, then they fall away when they face temptation.
8.14: The seeds that fell among the thorns represent those who hear the message, but all too quickly the message is crowded out by the cares and riches and pleasures of this life. And so they never grow into maturity.
8.15: And the seeds that fell on the good soil represent honest, good-hearted people who hear God’s word, cling to it, and patiently produce a huge harvest.
8.16: “No one lights a lamp and then covers it with a bowl or hides it under a bed. A lamp is placed on a stand, where its light can be seen by all who enter the house.
8.17: For all that is secret will eventually be brought into the open, and everything that is concealed will be brought to light and made known to all.
8.18: “So pay attention to how you hear. To those who listen to my teaching, more understanding will be given. But for those who are not listening, even what they think they understand will be taken away from them.”
8.19: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came to see him, but they couldn’t get to him because of the crowd.
8.20: Someone told Jesus, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, and they want to see you.”
8.21: Jesus replied, “My mother and my brothers are all those who hear God’s word and obey it.”
8.22: One day Jesus said to his disciples, “Let’s cross to the other side of the lake.” So they got into a boat and started out.
8.23: As they sailed across, Jesus settled down for a nap. But soon a fierce storm came down on the lake. The boat was filling with water, and they were in real danger.
8.24: The disciples went and woke him up, shouting, “Master, Master, we’re going to drown!” When Jesus woke up, he rebuked the wind and the raging waves. Suddenly the storm stopped and all was calm.
8.25: Then he asked them, “Where is your faith?” The disciples were terrified and amazed. “Who is this man?” they asked each other. “When he gives a command, even the wind and waves obey him!”
8.26: So they arrived in the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee.
8.27: As Jesus was climbing out of the boat, a man who was possessed by demons came out to meet him. For a long time he had been homeless and naked, living in the tombs outside the town.
8.28: As soon as he saw Jesus, he shrieked and fell down in front of him. Then he screamed, “Why are you interfering with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Please, I beg you, don’t torture me!”
8.29: For Jesus had already commanded the evil spirit to come out of him. This spirit had often taken control of the man. Even when he was placed under guard and put in chains and shackles, he simply broke them and rushed out into the wilderness, completely under the demon’s power.
8.30: Jesus demanded, “What is your name?” “Legion,” he replied, for he was filled with many demons.
8.31: The demons kept begging Jesus not to send them into the bottomless pit.
8.32: There happened to be a large herd of pigs feeding on the hillside nearby, and the demons begged him to let them enter into the pigs. So Jesus gave them permission.
8.33: Then the demons came out of the man and entered the pigs, and the entire herd plunged down the steep hillside into the lake and drowned.
8.34: When the herdsmen saw it, they fled to the nearby town and the surrounding countryside, spreading the news as they ran.
8.35: People rushed out to see what had happened. A crowd soon gathered around Jesus, and they saw the man who had been freed from the demons. He was sitting at Jesus’ feet, fully clothed and perfectly sane, and they were all afraid.
8.36: Then those who had seen what happened told the others how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
8.37: And all the people in the region of the Gerasenes begged Jesus to go away and leave them alone, for a great wave of fear swept over them. So Jesus returned to the boat and left, crossing back to the other side of the lake.
8.38: The man who had been freed from the demons begged to go with him. But Jesus sent him home, saying,
8.39: “No, go back to your family, and tell them everything God has done for you.” So he went all through the town proclaiming the great things Jesus had done for him.
8.40: On the other side of the lake the crowds welcomed Jesus, because they had been waiting for him.
8.41: Then a man named Jairus, a leader of the local synagogue, came and fell at Jesus’ feet, pleading with him to come home with him.
8.42: His only daughter, who was about twelve years old, was dying. As Jesus went with him, he was surrounded by the crowds.
8.43: A woman in the crowd had suffered for twelve years with constant bleeding, and she could find no cure.
8.44: Coming up behind Jesus, she touched the fringe of his robe. Immediately, the bleeding stopped.
8.45: “Who touched me?” Jesus asked. Everyone denied it, and Peter said, “Master, this whole crowd is pressing up against you.”
8.46: But Jesus said, “Someone deliberately touched me, for I felt healing power go out from me.”
8.47: When the woman realized that she could not stay hidden, she began to tremble and fell to her knees in front of him. The whole crowd heard her explain why she had touched him and that she had been immediately healed.
8.48: “Daughter,” he said to her, “your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
8.49: While he was still speaking to her, a messenger arrived from the home of Jairus, the leader of the synagogue. He told him, “Your daughter is dead. There’s no use troubling the Teacher now.”
8.50: But when Jesus heard what had happened, he said to Jairus, “Don’t be afraid. Just have faith, and she will be healed.”
8.51: When they arrived at the house, Jesus wouldn’t let anyone go in with him except Peter, John, James, and the little girl’s father and mother.
8.52: The house was filled with people weeping and wailing, but he said, “Stop the weeping! She isn’t dead; she’s only asleep.”
8.53: But the crowd laughed at him because they all knew she had died.
8.54: Then Jesus took her by the hand and said in a loud voice, “My child, get up!”
8.55: And at that moment her life returned, and she immediately stood up! Then Jesus told them to give her something to eat.
8.56: Her parents were overwhelmed, but Jesus insisted that they not tell anyone what had happened.

22.1: The Festival of Unleavened Bread, which is also called Passover, was approaching.
22.2: The leading priests and teachers of religious law were plotting how to kill Jesus, but they were afraid of the people’s reaction.
22.3: Then Satan entered into Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve disciples,
22.4: and he went to the leading priests and captains of the Temple guard to discuss the best way to betray Jesus to them.
22.5: They were delighted, and they promised to give him money.
22.6: So he agreed and began looking for an opportunity to betray Jesus so they could arrest him when the crowds weren’t around.
22.7: Now the Festival of Unleavened Bread arrived, when the Passover lamb is sacrificed.
22.8: Jesus sent Peter and John ahead and said, “Go and prepare the Passover meal, so we can eat it together.”
22.9: “Where do you want us to prepare it?” they asked him.
22.10: He replied, “As soon as you enter Jerusalem, a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him. At the house he enters,
22.11: say to the owner, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is the guest room where I can eat the Passover meal with my disciples?’
22.12: He will take you upstairs to a large room that is already set up. That is where you should prepare our meal.”
22.13: They went off to the city and found everything just as Jesus had said, and they prepared the Passover meal there.
22.14: When the time came, Jesus and the apostles sat down together at the table.
22.15: Jesus said, “I have been very eager to eat this Passover meal with you before my suffering begins.
22.16: For I tell you now that I won’t eat this meal again until its meaning is fulfilled in the Kingdom of God.”
22.17: Then he took a cup of wine and gave thanks to God for it. Then he said, “Take this and share it among yourselves.
22.18: For I will not drink wine again until the Kingdom of God has come.”
22.19: He took some bread and gave thanks to God for it. Then he broke it in pieces and gave it to the disciples, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”
22.20: After supper he took another cup of wine and said, “This cup is the new covenant between God and his people—an agreement confirmed with my blood, which is poured out as a sacrifice for you.
22.21: “But here at this table, sitting among us as a friend, is the man who will betray me.
22.22: For it has been determined that the Son of Man must die. But what sorrow awaits the one who betrays him.”
22.23: The disciples began to ask each other which of them would ever do such a thing.
22.24: Then they began to argue among themselves about who would be the greatest among them.
22.25: Jesus told them, “In this world the kings and great men lord it over their people, yet they are called ‘friends of the people.’
22.26: But among you it will be different. Those who are the greatest among you should take the lowest rank, and the leader should be like a servant.
22.27: Who is more important, the one who sits at the table or the one who serves? The one who sits at the table, of course. But not here! For I am among you as one who serves.
22.28: “You have stayed with me in my time of trial.
22.29: And just as my Father has granted me a Kingdom, I now grant you the right
22.30: to eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom. And you will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
22.31: “Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift each of you like wheat.
22.32: But I have pleaded in prayer for you, Simon, that your faith should not fail. So when you have repented and turned to me again, strengthen your brothers.”
22.33: Peter said, “Lord, I am ready to go to prison with you, and even to die with you.”
22.34: But Jesus said, “Peter, let me tell you something. Before the rooster crows tomorrow morning, you will deny three times that you even know me.”
22.35: Then Jesus asked them, “When I sent you out to preach the Good News and you did not have money, a traveler’s bag, or an extra pair of sandals, did you need anything?” “No,” they replied.
22.36: “But now,” he said, “take your money and a traveler’s bag. And if you don’t have a sword, sell your cloak and buy one!
22.37: For the time has come for this prophecy about me to be fulfilled: ‘He was counted among the rebels.’ Yes, everything written about me by the prophets will come true.”
22.38: “Look, Lord,” they replied, “we have two swords among us.” “That’s enough,” he said.
22.39: Then, accompanied by the disciples, Jesus left the upstairs room and went as usual to the Mount of Olives.
22.40: There he told them, “Pray that you will not give in to temptation.”
22.41: He walked away, about a stone’s throw, and knelt down and prayed,
22.42: “Father, if you are willing, please take this cup of suffering away from me. Yet I want your will to be done, not mine.”
22.43: Then an angel from heaven appeared and strengthened him.
22.44: He prayed more fervently, and he was in such agony of spirit that his sweat fell to the ground like great drops of blood.
22.45: At last he stood up again and returned to the disciples, only to find them asleep, exhausted from grief.
22.46: “Why are you sleeping?” he asked them. “Get up and pray, so that you will not give in to temptation.”
22.47: But even as Jesus said this, a crowd approached, led by Judas, one of the twelve disciples. Judas walked over to Jesus to greet him with a kiss.
22.48: But Jesus said, “Judas, would you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”
22.49: When the other disciples saw what was about to happen, they exclaimed, “Lord, should we fight? We brought the swords!”
22.50: And one of them struck at the high priest’s slave, slashing off his right ear.
22.51: But Jesus said, “No more of this.” And he touched the man’s ear and healed him.
22.52: Then Jesus spoke to the leading priests, the captains of the Temple guard, and the elders who had come for him. “Am I some dangerous revolutionary,” he asked, “that you come with swords and clubs to arrest me?
22.53: Why didn’t you arrest me in the Temple? I was there every day. But this is your moment, the time when the power of darkness reigns.”
22.54: So they arrested him and led him to the high priest’s home. And Peter followed at a distance.
22.55: The guards lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat around it, and Peter joined them there.
22.56: A servant girl noticed him in the firelight and began staring at him. Finally she said, “This man was one of Jesus’ followers!”
22.57: But Peter denied it. “Woman,” he said, “I don’t even know him!”
22.58: After a while someone else looked at him and said, “You must be one of them!” “No, man, I’m not!” Peter retorted.
22.59: About an hour later someone else insisted, “This must be one of them, because he is a Galilean, too.”
22.60: But Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you are talking about.” And immediately, while he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.
22.61: At that moment the Lord turned and looked at Peter. Suddenly, the Lord’s words flashed through Peter’s mind: “Before the rooster crows tomorrow morning, you will deny three times that you even know me.”
22.62: And Peter left the courtyard, weeping bitterly.
22.63: The guards in charge of Jesus began mocking and beating him.
22.64: They blindfolded him and said, “Prophesy to us! Who hit you that time?”
22.65: And they hurled all sorts of terrible insults at him.
22.66: At daybreak all the elders of the people assembled, including the leading priests and the teachers of religious law. Jesus was led before this high council,
22.67: and they said, “Tell us, are you the Messiah?” But he replied, “If I tell you, you won’t believe me.
22.68: And if I ask you a question, you won’t answer.
22.69: But from now on the Son of Man will be seated in the place of power at God’s right hand.”
22.70: They all shouted, “So, are you claiming to be the Son of God?” And he replied, “You say that I am.”
22.71: “Why do we need other witnesses?” they said. “We ourselves heard him say it.”

3.1: It was now the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius, the Roman emperor. Pontius Pilate was governor over Judea; Herod Antipas was ruler over Galilee; his brother Philip was ruler over Iturea and Traconitis; Lysanias was ruler over Abilene.
3.2: Annas and Caiaphas were the high priests. At this time a message from God came to John son of Zechariah, who was living in the wilderness.
3.3: Then John went from place to place on both sides of the Jordan River, preaching that people should be baptized to show that they had repented of their sins and turned to God to be forgiven.
3.4: Isaiah had spoken of John when he said, “He is a voice shouting in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord’s coming! Clear the road for him!
3.5: The valleys will be filled, and the mountains and hills made level. The curves will be straightened, and the rough places made smooth.
3.6: And then all people will see the salvation sent from God.’”
3.7: When the crowds came to John for baptism, he said, “You brood of snakes! Who warned you to flee the coming wrath?
3.8: Prove by the way you live that you have repented of your sins and turned to God. Don’t just say to each other, ‘We’re safe, for we are descendants of Abraham.’ That means nothing, for I tell you, God can create children of Abraham from these very stones.
3.9: Even now the ax of God’s judgment is poised, ready to sever the roots of the trees. Yes, every tree that does not produce good fruit will be chopped down and thrown into the fire.”
3.10: The crowds asked, “What should we do?”
3.11: John replied, “If you have two shirts, give one to the poor. If you have food, share it with those who are hungry.”
3.12: Even corrupt tax collectors came to be baptized and asked, “Teacher, what should we do?”
3.13: He replied, “Collect no more taxes than the government requires.”
3.14: “What should we do?” asked some soldiers. John replied, “Don’t extort money or make false accusations. And be content with your pay.”
3.15: Everyone was expecting the Messiah to come soon, and they were eager to know whether John might be the Messiah.
3.16: John answered their questions by saying, “I baptize you with water; but someone is coming soon who is greater than I am—so much greater that I’m not even worthy to be his slave and untie the straps of his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
3.17: He is ready to separate the chaff from the wheat with his winnowing fork. Then he will clean up the threshing area, gathering the wheat into his barn but burning the chaff with never-ending fire.”
3.18: John used many such warnings as he announced the Good News to the people.
3.19: John also publicly criticized Herod Antipas, the ruler of Galilee, for marrying Herodias, his brother’s wife, and for many other wrongs he had done.
3.20: So Herod put John in prison, adding this sin to his many others.
3.21: One day when the crowds were being baptized, Jesus himself was baptized. As he was praying, the heavens opened,
3.22: and the Holy Spirit, in bodily form, descended on him like a dove. And a voice from heaven said, “You are my dearly loved Son, and you bring me great joy.”
3.23: Jesus was about thirty years old when he began his public ministry. Jesus was known as the son of Joseph. Joseph was the son of Heli.
3.24: Heli was the son of Matthat. Matthat was the son of Levi. Levi was the son of Melki. Melki was the son of Jannai. Jannai was the son of Joseph.
3.25: Joseph was the son of Mattathias. Mattathias was the son of Amos. Amos was the son of Nahum. Nahum was the son of Esli. Esli was the son of Naggai.
3.26: Naggai was the son of Maath. Maath was the son of Mattathias. Mattathias was the son of Semein. Semein was the son of Josech. Josech was the son of Joda.
3.27: Joda was the son of Joanan. Joanan was the son of Rhesa. Rhesa was the son of Zerubbabel. Zerubbabel was the son of Shealtiel. Shealtiel was the son of Neri.
3.28: Neri was the son of Melki. Melki was the son of Addi. Addi was the son of Cosam. Cosam was the son of Elmadam. Elmadam was the son of Er.
3.29: Er was the son of Joshua. Joshua was the son of Eliezer. Eliezer was the son of Jorim. Jorim was the son of Matthat. Matthat was the son of Levi.
3.30: Levi was the son of Simeon. Simeon was the son of Judah. Judah was the son of Joseph. Joseph was the son of Jonam. Jonam was the son of Eliakim.
3.31: Eliakim was the son of Melea. Melea was the son of Menna. Menna was the son of Mattatha. Mattatha was the son of Nathan. Nathan was the son of David.
3.32: David was the son of Jesse. Jesse was the son of Obed. Obed was the son of Boaz. Boaz was the son of Salmon. Salmon was the son of Nahshon.
3.33: Nahshon was the son of Amminadab. Amminadab was the son of Admin. Admin was the son of Arni. Arni was the son of Hezron. Hezron was the son of Perez. Perez was the son of Judah.
3.34: Judah was the son of Jacob. Jacob was the son of Isaac. Isaac was the son of Abraham. Abraham was the son of Terah. Terah was the son of Nahor.
3.35: Nahor was the son of Serug. Serug was the son of Reu. Reu was the son of Peleg. Peleg was the son of Eber. Eber was the son of Shelah.
3.36: Shelah was the son of Cainan. Cainan was the son of Arphaxad. Arphaxad was the son of Shem. Shem was the son of Noah. Noah was the son of Lamech.
3.37: Lamech was the son of Methuselah. Methuselah was the son of Enoch. Enoch was the son of Jared. Jared was the son of Mahalalel. Mahalalel was the son of Kenan.
3.38: Kenan was the son of Enosh. Enosh was the son of Seth. Seth was the son of Adam. Adam was the son of God.

13.1: About this time Jesus was informed that Pilate had murdered some people from Galilee as they were offering sacrifices at the Temple.
13.2: “Do you think those Galileans were worse sinners than all the other people from Galilee?” Jesus asked. “Is that why they suffered?
13.3: Not at all! And you will perish, too, unless you repent of your sins and turn to God.
13.4: And what about the eighteen people who died when the tower in Siloam fell on them? Were they the worst sinners in Jerusalem?
13.5: No, and I tell you again that unless you repent, you will perish, too.”
13.6: Then Jesus told this story: “A man planted a fig tree in his garden and came again and again to see if there was any fruit on it, but he was always disappointed.
13.7: Finally, he said to his gardener, ‘I’ve waited three years, and there hasn’t been a single fig! Cut it down. It’s just taking up space in the garden.’
13.8: “The gardener answered, ‘Sir, give it one more chance. Leave it another year, and I’ll give it special attention and plenty of fertilizer.
13.9: If we get figs next year, fine. If not, then you can cut it down.’”
13.10: One Sabbath day as Jesus was teaching in a synagogue,
13.11: he saw a woman who had been crippled by an evil spirit. She had been bent double for eighteen years and was unable to stand up straight.
13.12: When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said, “Dear woman, you are healed of your sickness!”
13.13: Then he touched her, and instantly she could stand straight. How she praised God!
13.14: But the leader in charge of the synagogue was indignant that Jesus had healed her on the Sabbath day. “There are six days of the week for working,” he said to the crowd. “Come on those days to be healed, not on the Sabbath.”
13.15: But the Lord replied, “You hypocrites! Each of you works on the Sabbath day! Don’t you untie your ox or your donkey from its stall on the Sabbath and lead it out for water?
13.16: This dear woman, a daughter of Abraham, has been held in bondage by Satan for eighteen years. Isn’t it right that she be released, even on the Sabbath?”
13.17: This shamed his enemies, but all the people rejoiced at the wonderful things he did.
13.18: Then Jesus said, “What is the Kingdom of God like? How can I illustrate it?
13.19: It is like a tiny mustard seed that a man planted in a garden; it grows and becomes a tree, and the birds make nests in its branches.”
13.20: He also asked, “What else is the Kingdom of God like?
13.21: It is like the yeast a woman used in making bread. Even though she put only a little yeast in three measures of flour, it permeated every part of the dough.”
13.22: Jesus went through the towns and villages, teaching as he went, always pressing on toward Jerusalem.
13.23: Someone asked him, “Lord, will only a few be saved?” He replied,
13.24: “Work hard to enter the narrow door to God’s Kingdom, for many will try to enter but will fail.
13.25: When the master of the house has locked the door, it will be too late. You will stand outside knocking and pleading, ‘Lord, open the door for us!’ But he will reply, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’
13.26: Then you will say, ‘But we ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’
13.27: And he will reply, ‘I tell you, I don’t know you or where you come from. Get away from me, all you who do evil.’
13.28: “There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, for you will see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the Kingdom of God, but you will be thrown out.
13.29: And people will come from all over the world—from east and west, north and south—to take their places in the Kingdom of God.
13.30: And note this: Some who seem least important now will be the greatest then, and some who are the greatest now will be least important then.”
13.31: At that time some Pharisees said to him, “Get away from here if you want to live! Herod Antipas wants to kill you!”
13.32: Jesus replied, “Go tell that fox that I will keep on casting out demons and healing people today and tomorrow; and the third day I will accomplish my purpose.
13.33: Yes, today, tomorrow, and the next day I must proceed on my way. For it wouldn’t do for a prophet of God to be killed except in Jerusalem!
13.34: “O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones God’s messengers! How often I have wanted to gather your children together as a hen protects her chicks beneath her wings, but you wouldn’t let me.
13.35: And now, look, your house is abandoned. And you will never see me again until you say, ‘Blessings on the one who comes in the name of the Lord!’”

24.1: But very early on Sunday morning the women went to the tomb, taking the spices they had prepared.
24.2: They found that the stone had been rolled away from the entrance.
24.3: So they went in, but they didn’t find the body of the Lord Jesus.
24.4: As they stood there puzzled, two men suddenly appeared to them, clothed in dazzling robes.
24.5: The women were terrified and bowed with their faces to the ground. Then the men asked, “Why are you looking among the dead for someone who is alive?
24.6: He isn’t here! He is risen from the dead! Remember what he told you back in Galilee,
24.7: that the Son of Man must be betrayed into the hands of sinful men and be crucified, and that he would rise again on the third day.”
24.8: Then they remembered that he had said this.
24.9: So they rushed back from the tomb to tell his eleven disciples—and everyone else—what had happened.
24.10: It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and several other women who told the apostles what had happened.
24.11: But the story sounded like nonsense to the men, so they didn’t believe it.
24.12: However, Peter jumped up and ran to the tomb to look. Stooping, he peered in and saw the empty linen wrappings; then he went home again, wondering what had happened.
24.13: That same day two of Jesus’ followers were walking to the village of Emmaus, seven miles from Jerusalem.
24.14: As they walked along they were talking about everything that had happened.
24.15: As they talked and discussed these things, Jesus himself suddenly came and began walking with them.
24.16: But God kept them from recognizing him.
24.17: He asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?” They stopped short, sadness written across their faces.
24.18: Then one of them, Cleopas, replied, “You must be the only person in Jerusalem who hasn’t heard about all the things that have happened there the last few days.”
24.19: “What things?” Jesus asked. “The things that happened to Jesus, the man from Nazareth,” they said. “He was a prophet who did powerful miracles, and he was a mighty teacher in the eyes of God and all the people.
24.20: But our leading priests and other religious leaders handed him over to be condemned to death, and they crucified him.
24.21: We had hoped he was the Messiah who had come to rescue Israel. This all happened three days ago.
24.22: “Then some women from our group of his followers were at his tomb early this morning, and they came back with an amazing report.
24.23: They said his body was missing, and they had seen angels who told them Jesus is alive!
24.24: Some of our men ran out to see, and sure enough, his body was gone, just as the women had said.”
24.25: Then Jesus said to them, “You foolish people! You find it so hard to believe all that the prophets wrote in the Scriptures.
24.26: Wasn’t it clearly predicted that the Messiah would have to suffer all these things before entering his glory?”
24.27: Then Jesus took them through the writings of Moses and all the prophets, explaining from all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.
24.28: By this time they were nearing Emmaus and the end of their journey. Jesus acted as if he were going on,
24.29: but they begged him, “Stay the night with us, since it is getting late.” So he went home with them.
24.30: As they sat down to eat, he took the bread and blessed it. Then he broke it and gave it to them.
24.31: Suddenly, their eyes were opened, and they recognized him. And at that moment he disappeared!
24.32: They said to each other, “Didn’t our hearts burn within us as he talked with us on the road and explained the Scriptures to us?”
24.33: And within the hour they were on their way back to Jerusalem. There they found the eleven disciples and the others who had gathered with them,
24.34: who said, “The Lord has really risen! He appeared to Peter.”
24.35: Then the two from Emmaus told their story of how Jesus had appeared to them as they were walking along the road, and how they had recognized him as he was breaking the bread.
24.36: And just as they were telling about it, Jesus himself was suddenly standing there among them. “Peace be with you,” he said.
24.37: But the whole group was startled and frightened, thinking they were seeing a ghost!
24.38: “Why are you frightened?” he asked. “Why are your hearts filled with doubt?
24.39: Look at my hands. Look at my feet. You can see that it’s really me. Touch me and make sure that I am not a ghost, because ghosts don’t have bodies, as you see that I do.”
24.40: As he spoke, he showed them his hands and his feet.
24.41: Still they stood there in disbelief, filled with joy and wonder. Then he asked them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
24.42: They gave him a piece of broiled fish,
24.43: and he ate it as they watched.
24.44: Then he said, “When I was with you before, I told you that everything written about me in the law of Moses and the prophets and in the Psalms must be fulfilled.”
24.45: Then he opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
24.46: And he said, “Yes, it was written long ago that the Messiah would suffer and die and rise from the dead on the third day.
24.47: It was also written that this message would be proclaimed in the authority of his name to all the nations, beginning in Jerusalem: ‘There is forgiveness of sins for all who repent.’
24.48: You are witnesses of all these things.
24.49: “And now I will send the Holy Spirit, just as my Father promised. But stay here in the city until the Holy Spirit comes and fills you with power from heaven.”
24.50: Then Jesus led them to Bethany, and lifting his hands to heaven, he blessed them.
24.51: While he was blessing them, he left them and was taken up to heaven.
24.52: So they worshiped him and then returned to Jerusalem filled with great joy.
24.53: And they spent all of their time in the Temple, praising God.

12.1: Meanwhile, the crowds grew until thousands were milling about and stepping on each other. Jesus turned first to his disciples and warned them, “Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees—their hypocrisy.
12.2: The time is coming when everything that is covered up will be revealed, and all that is secret will be made known to all.
12.3: Whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered behind closed doors will be shouted from the housetops for all to hear!
12.4: “Dear friends, don’t be afraid of those who want to kill your body; they cannot do any more to you after that.
12.5: But I’ll tell you whom to fear. Fear God, who has the power to kill you and then throw you into hell. Yes, he’s the one to fear.
12.6: “What is the price of five sparrows—two copper coins? Yet God does not forget a single one of them.
12.7: And the very hairs on your head are all numbered. So don’t be afraid; you are more valuable to God than a whole flock of sparrows.
12.8: “I tell you the truth, everyone who acknowledges me publicly here on earth, the Son of Man will also acknowledge in the presence of God’s angels.
12.9: But anyone who denies me here on earth will be denied before God’s angels.
12.10: Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man can be forgiven, but anyone who blasphemes the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
12.11: “And when you are brought to trial in the synagogues and before rulers and authorities, don’t worry about how to defend yourself or what to say,
12.12: for the Holy Spirit will teach you at that time what needs to be said.”
12.13: Then someone called from the crowd, “Teacher, please tell my brother to divide our father’s estate with me.”
12.14: Jesus replied, “Friend, who made me a judge over you to decide such things as that?”
12.15: Then he said, “Beware! Guard against every kind of greed. Life is not measured by how much you own.”
12.16: Then he told them a story: “A rich man had a fertile farm that produced fine crops.
12.17: He said to himself, ‘What should I do? I don’t have room for all my crops.’
12.18: Then he said, ‘I know! I’ll tear down my barns and build bigger ones. Then I’ll have room enough to store all my wheat and other goods.
12.19: And I’ll sit back and say to myself, “My friend, you have enough stored away for years to come. Now take it easy! Eat, drink, and be merry!”’
12.20: “But God said to him, ‘You fool! You will die this very night. Then who will get everything you worked for?’
12.21: “Yes, a person is a fool to store up earthly wealth but not have a rich relationship with God.”
12.22: Then, turning to his disciples, Jesus said, “That is why I tell you not to worry about everyday life—whether you have enough food to eat or enough clothes to wear.
12.23: For life is more than food, and your body more than clothing.
12.24: Look at the ravens. They don’t plant or harvest or store food in barns, for God feeds them. And you are far more valuable to him than any birds!
12.25: Can all your worries add a single moment to your life?
12.26: And if worry can’t accomplish a little thing like that, what’s the use of worrying over bigger things?
12.27: “Look at the lilies and how they grow. They don’t work or make their clothing, yet Solomon in all his glory was not dressed as beautifully as they are.
12.28: And if God cares so wonderfully for flowers that are here today and thrown into the fire tomorrow, he will certainly care for you. Why do you have so little faith?
12.29: “And don’t be concerned about what to eat and what to drink. Don’t worry about such things.
12.30: These things dominate the thoughts of unbelievers all over the world, but your Father already knows your needs.
12.31: Seek the Kingdom of God above all else, and he will give you everything you need.
12.32: “So don’t be afraid, little flock. For it gives your Father great happiness to give you the Kingdom.
12.33: “Sell your possessions and give to those in need. This will store up treasure for you in heaven! And the purses of heaven never get old or develop holes. Your treasure will be safe; no thief can steal it and no moth can destroy it.
12.34: Wherever your treasure is, there the desires of your heart will also be.
12.35: “Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning,
12.36: as though you were waiting for your master to return from the wedding feast. Then you will be ready to open the door and let him in the moment he arrives and knocks.
12.37: The servants who are ready and waiting for his return will be rewarded. I tell you the truth, he himself will seat them, put on an apron, and serve them as they sit and eat!
12.38: He may come in the middle of the night or just before dawn. But whenever he comes, he will reward the servants who are ready.
12.39: “Understand this: If a homeowner knew exactly when a burglar was coming, he would not permit his house to be broken into.
12.40: You also must be ready all the time, for the Son of Man will come when least expected.”
12.41: Peter asked, “Lord, is that illustration just for us or for everyone?”
12.42: And the Lord replied, “A faithful, sensible servant is one to whom the master can give the responsibility of managing his other household servants and feeding them.
12.43: If the master returns and finds that the servant has done a good job, there will be a reward.
12.44: I tell you the truth, the master will put that servant in charge of all he owns.
12.45: But what if the servant thinks, ‘My master won’t be back for a while,’ and he begins beating the other servants, partying, and getting drunk?
12.46: The master will return unannounced and unexpected, and he will cut the servant in pieces and banish him with the unfaithful.
12.47: “And a servant who knows what the master wants, but isn’t prepared and doesn’t carry out those instructions, will be severely punished.
12.48: But someone who does not know, and then does something wrong, will be punished only lightly. When someone has been given much, much will be required in return; and when someone has been entrusted with much, even more will be required.
12.49: “I have come to set the world on fire, and I wish it were already burning!
12.50: I have a terrible baptism of suffering ahead of me, and I am under a heavy burden until it is accomplished.
12.51: Do you think I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I have come to divide people against each other!
12.52: From now on families will be split apart, three in favor of me, and two against—or two in favor and three against.
12.53: ‘Father will be divided against son and son against father; mother against daughter and daughter against mother; and mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.’”
12.54: Then Jesus turned to the crowd and said, “When you see clouds beginning to form in the west, you say, ‘Here comes a shower.’ And you are right.
12.55: When the south wind blows, you say, ‘Today will be a scorcher.’ And it is.
12.56: You fools! You know how to interpret the weather signs of the earth and sky, but you don’t know how to interpret the present times.
12.57: “Why can’t you decide for yourselves what is right?
12.58: When you are on the way to court with your accuser, try to settle the matter before you get there. Otherwise, your accuser may drag you before the judge, who will hand you over to an officer, who will throw you into prison.
12.59: And if that happens, you won’t be free again until you have paid the very last penny.”

2.1: At that time the Roman emperor, Augustus, decreed that a census should be taken throughout the Roman Empire.
2.2: (This was the first census taken when Quirinius was governor of Syria.)
2.3: All returned to their own ancestral towns to register for this census.
2.4: And because Joseph was a descendant of King David, he had to go to Bethlehem in Judea, David’s ancient home. He traveled there from the village of Nazareth in Galilee.
2.5: He took with him Mary, to whom he was engaged, who was now expecting a child.
2.6: And while they were there, the time came for her baby to be born.
2.7: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him snugly in strips of cloth and laid him in a manger, because there was no lodging available for them.
2.8: That night there were shepherds staying in the fields nearby, guarding their flocks of sheep.
2.9: Suddenly, an angel of the Lord appeared among them, and the radiance of the Lord’s glory surrounded them. They were terrified,
2.10: but the angel reassured them. “Don’t be afraid!” he said. “I bring you good news that will bring great joy to all people.
2.11: The Savior—yes, the Messiah, the Lord—has been born today in Bethlehem, the city of David!
2.12: And you will recognize him by this sign: You will find a baby wrapped snugly in strips of cloth, lying in a manger.”
2.13: Suddenly, the angel was joined by a vast host of others—the armies of heaven—praising God and saying,
2.14: “Glory to God in highest heaven, and peace on earth to those with whom God is pleased.”
2.15: When the angels had returned to heaven, the shepherds said to each other, “Let’s go to Bethlehem! Let’s see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has told us about.”
2.16: They hurried to the village and found Mary and Joseph. And there was the baby, lying in the manger.
2.17: After seeing him, the shepherds told everyone what had happened and what the angel had said to them about this child.
2.18: All who heard the shepherds’ story were astonished,
2.19: but Mary kept all these things in her heart and thought about them often.
2.20: The shepherds went back to their flocks, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen. It was just as the angel had told them.
2.21: Eight days later, when the baby was circumcised, he was named Jesus, the name given him by the angel even before he was conceived.
2.22: Then it was time for their purification offering, as required by the law of Moses after the birth of a child; so his parents took him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord.
2.23: The law of the Lord says, “If a woman’s first child is a boy, he must be dedicated to the Lord.”
2.24: So they offered the sacrifice required in the law of the Lord—“either a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
2.25: At that time there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. He was righteous and devout and was eagerly waiting for the Messiah to come and rescue Israel. The Holy Spirit was upon him
2.26: and had revealed to him that he would not die until he had seen the Lord’s Messiah.
2.27: That day the Spirit led him to the Temple. So when Mary and Joseph came to present the baby Jesus to the Lord as the law required,
2.28: Simeon was there. He took the child in his arms and praised God, saying,
2.29: “Sovereign Lord, now let your servant die in peace, as you have promised.
2.31: which you have prepared for all people.
2.32: He is a light to reveal God to the nations, and he is the glory of your people Israel!”
2.33: Jesus’ parents were amazed at what was being said about him.
2.34: Then Simeon blessed them, and he said to Mary, the baby’s mother, “This child is destined to cause many in Israel to fall, and many others to rise. He has been sent as a sign from God, but many will oppose him.
2.35: As a result, the deepest thoughts of many hearts will be revealed. And a sword will pierce your very soul.”
2.36: Anna, a prophet, was also there in the Temple. She was the daughter of Phanuel from the tribe of Asher, and she was very old. Her husband died when they had been married only seven years.
2.37: Then she lived as a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the Temple but stayed there day and night, worshiping God with fasting and prayer.
2.38: She came along just as Simeon was talking with Mary and Joseph, and she began praising God. She talked about the child to everyone who had been waiting expectantly for God to rescue Jerusalem.
2.39: When Jesus’ parents had fulfilled all the requirements of the law of the Lord, they returned home to Nazareth in Galilee.
2.40: There the child grew up healthy and strong. He was filled with wisdom, and God’s favor was on him.
2.41: Every year Jesus’ parents went to Jerusalem for the Passover festival.
2.42: When Jesus was twelve years old, they attended the festival as usual.
2.43: After the celebration was over, they started home to Nazareth, but Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. His parents didn’t miss him at first,
2.44: because they assumed he was among the other travelers. But when he didn’t show up that evening, they started looking for him among their relatives and friends.
2.45: When they couldn’t find him, they went back to Jerusalem to search for him there.
2.46: Three days later they finally discovered him in the Temple, sitting among the religious teachers, listening to them and asking questions.
2.47: All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
2.48: His parents didn’t know what to think. “Son,” his mother said to him, “why have you done this to us? Your father and I have been frantic, searching for you everywhere.”
2.49: “But why did you need to search?” he asked. “Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?”
2.50: But they didn’t understand what he meant.
2.51: Then he returned to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them. And his mother stored all these things in her heart.
2.52: Jesus grew in wisdom and in stature and in favor with God and all the people.

11.1: Once Jesus was in a certain place praying. As he finished, one of his disciples came to him and said, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”
11.2: Jesus said, “This is how you should pray: “Father, may your name be kept holy. May your Kingdom come soon.
11.3: Give us each day the food we need,
11.4: and forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us. And don’t let us yield to temptation.”
11.5: Then, teaching them more about prayer, he used this story: “Suppose you went to a friend’s house at midnight, wanting to borrow three loaves of bread. You say to him,
11.6: ‘A friend of mine has just arrived for a visit, and I have nothing for him to eat.’
11.7: And suppose he calls out from his bedroom, ‘Don’t bother me. The door is locked for the night, and my family and I are all in bed. I can’t help you.’
11.8: But I tell you this—though he won’t do it for friendship’s sake, if you keep knocking long enough, he will get up and give you whatever you need because of your shameless persistence.
11.9: “And so I tell you, keep on asking, and you will receive what you ask for. Keep on seeking, and you will find. Keep on knocking, and the door will be opened to you.
11.10: For everyone who asks, receives. Everyone who seeks, finds. And to everyone who knocks, the door will be opened.
11.11: “You fathers—if your children ask for a fish, do you give them a snake instead?
11.12: Or if they ask for an egg, do you give them a scorpion? Of course not!
11.13: So if you sinful people know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him.”
11.14: One day Jesus cast out a demon from a man who couldn’t speak, and when the demon was gone, the man began to speak. The crowds were amazed,
11.15: but some of them said, “No wonder he can cast out demons. He gets his power from Satan, the prince of demons.”
11.16: Others, trying to test Jesus, demanded that he show them a miraculous sign from heaven to prove his authority.
11.17: He knew their thoughts, so he said, “Any kingdom divided by civil war is doomed. A family splintered by feuding will fall apart.
11.18: You say I am empowered by Satan. But if Satan is divided and fighting against himself, how can his kingdom survive?
11.19: And if I am empowered by Satan, what about your own exorcists? They cast out demons, too, so they will condemn you for what you have said.
11.20: But if I am casting out demons by the power of God, then the Kingdom of God has arrived among you.
11.21: For when a strong man is fully armed and guards his palace, his possessions are safe—
11.22: until someone even stronger attacks and overpowers him, strips him of his weapons, and carries off his belongings.
11.23: “Anyone who isn’t with me opposes me, and anyone who isn’t working with me is actually working against me.
11.24: “When an evil spirit leaves a person, it goes into the desert, searching for rest. But when it finds none, it says, ‘I will return to the person I came from.’
11.25: So it returns and finds that its former home is all swept and in order.
11.26: Then the spirit finds seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they all enter the person and live there. And so that person is worse off than before.”
11.27: As he was speaking, a woman in the crowd called out, “God bless your mother—the womb from which you came, and the breasts that nursed you!”
11.28: Jesus replied, “But even more blessed are all who hear the word of God and put it into practice.”
11.29: As the crowd pressed in on Jesus, he said, “This evil generation keeps asking me to show them a miraculous sign. But the only sign I will give them is the sign of Jonah.
11.30: What happened to him was a sign to the people of Nineveh that God had sent him. What happens to the Son of Man will be a sign to these people that he was sent by God.
11.31: “The queen of Sheba will stand up against this generation on judgment day and condemn it, for she came from a distant land to hear the wisdom of Solomon. Now someone greater than Solomon is here—but you refuse to listen.
11.32: The people of Nineveh will also stand up against this generation on judgment day and condemn it, for they repented of their sins at the preaching of Jonah. Now someone greater than Jonah is here—but you refuse to repent.
11.33: “No one lights a lamp and then hides it or puts it under a basket. Instead, a lamp is placed on a stand, where its light can be seen by all who enter the house.
11.34: “Your eye is like a lamp that provides light for your body. When your eye is healthy, your whole body is filled with light. But when it is unhealthy, your body is filled with darkness.
11.35: Make sure that the light you think you have is not actually darkness.
11.36: If you are filled with light, with no dark corners, then your whole life will be radiant, as though a floodlight were filling you with light.”
11.37: As Jesus was speaking, one of the Pharisees invited him home for a meal. So he went in and took his place at the table.
11.38: His host was amazed to see that he sat down to eat without first performing the hand-washing ceremony required by Jewish custom.
11.39: Then the Lord said to him, “You Pharisees are so careful to clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are filthy—full of greed and wickedness!
11.40: Fools! Didn’t God make the inside as well as the outside?
11.41: So clean the inside by giving gifts to the poor, and you will be clean all over.
11.42: “What sorrow awaits you Pharisees! For you are careful to tithe even the tiniest income from your herb gardens, but you ignore justice and the love of God. You should tithe, yes, but do not neglect the more important things.
11.43: “What sorrow awaits you Pharisees! For you love to sit in the seats of honor in the synagogues and receive respectful greetings as you walk in the marketplaces.
11.44: Yes, what sorrow awaits you! For you are like hidden graves in a field. People walk over them without knowing the corruption they are stepping on.”
11.45: “Teacher,” said an expert in religious law, “you have insulted us, too, in what you just said.”
11.46: “Yes,” said Jesus, “what sorrow also awaits you experts in religious law! For you crush people with unbearable religious demands, and you never lift a finger to ease the burden.
11.47: What sorrow awaits you! For you build monuments for the prophets your own ancestors killed long ago.
11.48: But in fact, you stand as witnesses who agree with what your ancestors did. They killed the prophets, and you join in their crime by building the monuments!
11.49: This is what God in his wisdom said about you: ‘I will send prophets and apostles to them, but they will kill some and persecute the others.’
11.50: “As a result, this generation will be held responsible for the murder of all God’s prophets from the creation of the world—
11.51: from the murder of Abel to the murder of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, it will certainly be charged against this generation.
11.52: “What sorrow awaits you experts in religious law! For you remove the key to knowledge from the people. You don’t enter the Kingdom yourselves, and you prevent others from entering.”
11.53: As Jesus was leaving, the teachers of religious law and the Pharisees became hostile and tried to provoke him with many questions.
11.54: They wanted to trap him into saying something they could use against him.

1.1: Many people have set out to write accounts about the events that have been fulfilled among us.
1.2: They used the eyewitness reports circulating among us from the early disciples.
1.3: Having carefully investigated everything from the beginning, I also have decided to write an accurate account for you, most honorable Theophilus,
1.4: so you can be certain of the truth of everything you were taught.
1.5: When Herod was king of Judea, there was a Jewish priest named Zechariah. He was a member of the priestly order of Abijah, and his wife, Elizabeth, was also from the priestly line of Aaron.
1.6: Zechariah and Elizabeth were righteous in God’s eyes, careful to obey all of the Lord’s commandments and regulations.
1.7: They had no children because Elizabeth was unable to conceive, and they were both very old.
1.8: One day Zechariah was serving God in the Temple, for his order was on duty that week.
1.9: As was the custom of the priests, he was chosen by lot to enter the sanctuary of the Lord and burn incense.
1.10: While the incense was being burned, a great crowd stood outside, praying.
1.11: While Zechariah was in the sanctuary, an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the incense altar.
1.12: Zechariah was shaken and overwhelmed with fear when he saw him.
1.13: But the angel said, “Don’t be afraid, Zechariah! God has heard your prayer. Your wife, Elizabeth, will give you a son, and you are to name him John.
1.14: You will have great joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth,
1.15: for he will be great in the eyes of the Lord. He must never touch wine or other alcoholic drinks. He will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even before his birth.
1.16: And he will turn many Israelites to the Lord their God.
1.17: He will be a man with the spirit and power of Elijah. He will prepare the people for the coming of the Lord. He will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children, and he will cause those who are rebellious to accept the wisdom of the godly.”
1.18: Zechariah said to the angel, “How can I be sure this will happen? I’m an old man now, and my wife is also well along in years.”
1.19: Then the angel said, “I am Gabriel! I stand in the very presence of God. It was he who sent me to bring you this good news!
1.20: But now, since you didn’t believe what I said, you will be silent and unable to speak until the child is born. For my words will certainly be fulfilled at the proper time.”
1.21: Meanwhile, the people were waiting for Zechariah to come out of the sanctuary, wondering why he was taking so long.
1.22: When he finally did come out, he couldn’t speak to them. Then they realized from his gestures and his silence that he must have seen a vision in the sanctuary.
1.23: When Zechariah’s week of service in the Temple was over, he returned home.
1.24: Soon afterward his wife, Elizabeth, became pregnant and went into seclusion for five months.
1.25: “How kind the Lord is!” she exclaimed. “He has taken away my disgrace of having no children.”
1.26: In the sixth month of Elizabeth’s pregnancy, God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth, a village in Galilee,
1.27: to a virgin named Mary. She was engaged to be married to a man named Joseph, a descendant of King David.
1.28: Gabriel appeared to her and said, “Greetings, favored woman! The Lord is with you!”
1.29: Confused and disturbed, Mary tried to think what the angel could mean.
1.30: “Don’t be afraid, Mary,” the angel told her, “for you have found favor with God!
1.31: You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus.
1.32: He will be very great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his ancestor David.
1.33: And he will reign over Israel forever; his Kingdom will never end!”
1.34: Mary asked the angel, “But how can this happen? I am a virgin.”
1.35: The angel replied, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the baby to be born will be holy, and he will be called the Son of God.
1.36: What’s more, your relative Elizabeth has become pregnant in her old age! People used to say she was barren, but she has conceived a son and is now in her sixth month.
1.37: For the word of God will never fail.”
1.38: Mary responded, “I am the Lord’s servant. May everything you have said about me come true.” And then the angel left her.
1.39: A few days later Mary hurried to the hill country of Judea, to the town
1.40: where Zechariah lived. She entered the house and greeted Elizabeth.
1.41: At the sound of Mary’s greeting, Elizabeth’s child leaped within her, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
1.42: Elizabeth gave a glad cry and exclaimed to Mary, “God has blessed you above all women, and your child is blessed.
1.43: Why am I so honored, that the mother of my Lord should visit me?
1.44: When I heard your greeting, the baby in my womb jumped for joy.
1.45: You are blessed because you believed that the Lord would do what he said.”
1.46: Mary responded, “Oh, how my soul praises the Lord.
1.47: How my spirit rejoices in God my Savior!
1.48: For he took notice of his lowly servant girl, and from now on all generations will call me blessed.
1.49: For the Mighty One is holy, and he has done great things for me.
1.50: He shows mercy from generation to generation to all who fear him.
1.51: His mighty arm has done tremendous things! He has scattered the proud and haughty ones.
1.52: He has brought down princes from their thrones and exalted the humble.
1.53: He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away with empty hands.
1.54: He has helped his servant Israel and remembered to be merciful.
1.55: For he made this promise to our ancestors, to Abraham and his children forever.”
1.56: Mary stayed with Elizabeth about three months and then went back to her own home.
1.57: When it was time for Elizabeth’s baby to be born, she gave birth to a son.
1.58: And when her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had been very merciful to her, everyone rejoiced with her.
1.59: When the baby was eight days old, they all came for the circumcision ceremony. They wanted to name him Zechariah, after his father.
1.60: But Elizabeth said, “No! His name is John!”
1.61: “What?” they exclaimed. “There is no one in all your family by that name.”
1.62: So they used gestures to ask the baby’s father what he wanted to name him.
1.63: He motioned for a writing tablet, and to everyone’s surprise he wrote, “His name is John.”
1.64: Instantly Zechariah could speak again, and he began praising God.
1.65: Awe fell upon the whole neighborhood, and the news of what had happened spread throughout the Judean hills.
1.66: Everyone who heard about it reflected on these events and asked, “What will this child turn out to be?” For the hand of the Lord was surely upon him in a special way.
1.67: Then his father, Zechariah, was filled with the Holy Spirit and gave this prophecy:
1.68: “Praise the Lord, the God of Israel, because he has visited and redeemed his people.
1.69: He has sent us a mighty Savior from the royal line of his servant David,
1.70: just as he promised through his holy prophets long ago.
1.71: Now we will be saved from our enemies and from all who hate us.
1.72: He has been merciful to our ancestors by remembering his sacred covenant—
1.73: the covenant he swore with an oath to our ancestor Abraham.
1.74: We have been rescued from our enemies so we can serve God without fear,
1.75: in holiness and righteousness for as long as we live.
1.76: “And you, my little son, will be called the prophet of the Most High, because you will prepare the way for the Lord.
1.77: You will tell his people how to find salvation through forgiveness of their sins.
1.78: Because of God’s tender mercy, the morning light from heaven is about to break upon us,
1.79: to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, and to guide us to the path of peace.”
1.80: John grew up and became strong in spirit. And he lived in the wilderness until he began his public ministry to Israel.

10.1: The Lord now chose seventy-two other disciples and sent them ahead in pairs to all the towns and places he planned to visit.
10.2: These were his instructions to them: “The harvest is great, but the workers are few. So pray to the Lord who is in charge of the harvest; ask him to send more workers into his fields.
10.3: Now go, and remember that I am sending you out as lambs among wolves.
10.4: Don’t take any money with you, nor a traveler’s bag, nor an extra pair of sandals. And don’t stop to greet anyone on the road.
10.5: “Whenever you enter someone’s home, first say, ‘May God’s peace be on this house.’
10.6: If those who live there are peaceful, the blessing will stand; if they are not, the blessing will return to you.
10.7: Don’t move around from home to home. Stay in one place, eating and drinking what they provide. Don’t hesitate to accept hospitality, because those who work deserve their pay.
10.8: “If you enter a town and it welcomes you, eat whatever is set before you.
10.9: Heal the sick, and tell them, ‘The Kingdom of God is near you now.’
10.10: But if a town refuses to welcome you, go out into its streets and say,
10.11: ‘We wipe even the dust of your town from our feet to show that we have abandoned you to your fate. And know this—the Kingdom of God is near!’
10.12: I assure you, even wicked Sodom will be better off than such a town on judgment day.
10.13: “What sorrow awaits you, Korazin and Bethsaida! For if the miracles I did in you had been done in wicked Tyre and Sidon, their people would have repented of their sins long ago, clothing themselves in burlap and throwing ashes on their heads to show their remorse.
10.14: Yes, Tyre and Sidon will be better off on judgment day than you.
10.15: And you people of Capernaum, will you be honored in heaven? No, you will go down to the place of the dead.”
10.16: Then he said to the disciples, “Anyone who accepts your message is also accepting me. And anyone who rejects you is rejecting me. And anyone who rejects me is rejecting God, who sent me.”
10.17: When the seventy-two disciples returned, they joyfully reported to him, “Lord, even the demons obey us when we use your name!”
10.18: “Yes,” he told them, “I saw Satan fall from heaven like lightning!
10.19: Look, I have given you authority over all the power of the enemy, and you can walk among snakes and scorpions and crush them. Nothing will injure you.
10.20: But don’t rejoice because evil spirits obey you; rejoice because your names are registered in heaven.”
10.21: At that same time Jesus was filled with the joy of the Holy Spirit, and he said, “O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, thank you for hiding these things from those who think themselves wise and clever, and for revealing them to the childlike. Yes, Father, it pleased you to do it this way.
10.22: “My Father has entrusted everything to me. No one truly knows the Son except the Father, and no one truly knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.”
10.23: Then when they were alone, he turned to the disciples and said, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you have seen.
10.24: I tell you, many prophets and kings longed to see what you see, but they didn’t see it. And they longed to hear what you hear, but they didn’t hear it.”
10.25: One day an expert in religious law stood up to test Jesus by asking him this question: “Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life?”
10.26: Jesus replied, “What does the law of Moses say? How do you read it?”
10.27: The man answered, “‘You must love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, all your strength, and all your mind.’ And, ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
10.28: “Right!” Jesus told him. “Do this and you will live!”
10.29: The man wanted to justify his actions, so he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
10.30: Jesus replied with a story: “A Jewish man was traveling from Jerusalem down to Jericho, and he was attacked by bandits. They stripped him of his clothes, beat him up, and left him half dead beside the road.
10.31: “By chance a priest came along. But when he saw the man lying there, he crossed to the other side of the road and passed him by.
10.32: A Temple assistant walked over and looked at him lying there, but he also passed by on the other side.
10.33: “Then a despised Samaritan came along, and when he saw the man, he felt compassion for him.
10.34: Going over to him, the Samaritan soothed his wounds with olive oil and wine and bandaged them. Then he put the man on his own donkey and took him to an inn, where he took care of him.
10.35: The next day he handed the innkeeper two silver coins, telling him, ‘Take care of this man. If his bill runs higher than this, I’ll pay you the next time I’m here.’
10.36: “Now which of these three would you say was a neighbor to the man who was attacked by bandits?” Jesus asked.
10.37: The man replied, “The one who showed him mercy.” Then Jesus said, “Yes, now go and do the same.”
10.38: As Jesus and the disciples continued on their way to Jerusalem, they came to a certain village where a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home.
10.39: Her sister, Mary, sat at the Lord’s feet, listening to what he taught.
10.40: But Martha was distracted by the big dinner she was preparing. She came to Jesus and said, “Lord, doesn’t it seem unfair to you that my sister just sits here while I do all the work? Tell her to come and help me.”
10.41: But the Lord said to her, “My dear Martha, you are worried and upset over all these details!
10.42: There is only one thing worth being concerned about. Mary has discovered it, and it will not be taken away from her.”

21.1: While Jesus was in the Temple, he watched the rich people dropping their gifts in the collection box.
21.2: Then a poor widow came by and dropped in two small coins.
21.3: “I tell you the truth,” Jesus said, “this poor widow has given more than all the rest of them.
21.4: For they have given a tiny part of their surplus, but she, poor as she is, has given everything she has.”
21.5: Some of his disciples began talking about the majestic stonework of the Temple and the memorial decorations on the walls. But Jesus said,
21.6: “The time is coming when all these things will be completely demolished. Not one stone will be left on top of another!”
21.7: “Teacher,” they asked, “when will all this happen? What sign will show us that these things are about to take place?”
21.8: He replied, “Don’t let anyone mislead you, for many will come in my name, claiming, ‘I am the Messiah,’ and saying, ‘The time has come!’ But don’t believe them.
21.9: And when you hear of wars and insurrections, don’t panic. Yes, these things must take place first, but the end won’t follow immediately.”
21.10: Then he added, “Nation will go to war against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
21.11: There will be great earthquakes, and there will be famines and plagues in many lands, and there will be terrifying things and great miraculous signs from heaven.
21.12: “But before all this occurs, there will be a time of great persecution. You will be dragged into synagogues and prisons, and you will stand trial before kings and governors because you are my followers.
21.13: But this will be your opportunity to tell them about me.
21.14: So don’t worry in advance about how to answer the charges against you,
21.15: for I will give you the right words and such wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to reply or refute you!
21.16: Even those closest to you—your parents, brothers, relatives, and friends—will betray you. They will even kill some of you.
21.17: And everyone will hate you because you are my followers.
21.18: But not a hair of your head will perish!
21.19: By standing firm, you will win your souls.
21.20: “And when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then you will know that the time of its destruction has arrived.
21.21: Then those in Judea must flee to the hills. Those in Jerusalem must get out, and those out in the country should not return to the city.
21.22: For those will be days of God’s vengeance, and the prophetic words of the Scriptures will be fulfilled.
21.23: How terrible it will be for pregnant women and for nursing mothers in those days. For there will be disaster in the land and great anger against this people.
21.24: They will be killed by the sword or sent away as captives to all the nations of the world. And Jerusalem will be trampled down by the Gentiles until the period of the Gentiles comes to an end.
21.25: “And there will be strange signs in the sun, moon, and stars. And here on earth the nations will be in turmoil, perplexed by the roaring seas and strange tides.
21.26: People will be terrified at what they see coming upon the earth, for the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
21.27: Then everyone will see the Son of Man coming on a cloud with power and great glory.
21.28: So when all these things begin to happen, stand and look up, for your salvation is near!”
21.29: Then he gave them this illustration: “Notice the fig tree, or any other tree.
21.30: When the leaves come out, you know without being told that summer is near.
21.31: In the same way, when you see all these things taking place, you can know that the Kingdom of God is near.
21.32: I tell you the truth, this generation will not pass from the scene until all these things have taken place.
21.33: Heaven and earth will disappear, but my words will never disappear.
21.34: “Watch out! Don’t let your hearts be dulled by carousing and drunkenness, and by the worries of this life. Don’t let that day catch you unaware,
21.35: like a trap. For that day will come upon everyone living on the earth.
21.36: Keep alert at all times. And pray that you might be strong enough to escape these coming horrors and stand before the Son of Man.”
21.37: Every day Jesus went to the Temple to teach, and each evening he returned to spend the night on the Mount of Olives.
21.38: The crowds gathered at the Temple early each morning to hear him.

17.1: One day Jesus said to his disciples, “There will always be temptations to sin, but what sorrow awaits the person who does the tempting!
17.2: It would be better to be thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around your neck than to cause one of these little ones to fall into sin.
17.3: So watch yourselves! “If another believer sins, rebuke that person; then if there is repentance, forgive.
17.4: Even if that person wrongs you seven times a day and each time turns again and asks forgiveness, you must forgive.”
17.5: The apostles said to the Lord, “Show us how to increase our faith.”
17.6: The Lord answered, “If you had faith even as small as a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, ‘May you be uprooted and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you!
17.7: “When a servant comes in from plowing or taking care of sheep, does his master say, ‘Come in and eat with me’?
17.8: No, he says, ‘Prepare my meal, put on your apron, and serve me while I eat. Then you can eat later.’
17.9: And does the master thank the servant for doing what he was told to do? Of course not.
17.10: In the same way, when you obey me you should say, ‘We are unworthy servants who have simply done our duty.’”
17.11: As Jesus continued on toward Jerusalem, he reached the border between Galilee and Samaria.
17.12: As he entered a village there, ten men with leprosy stood at a distance,
17.13: crying out, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
17.14: He looked at them and said, “Go show yourselves to the priests.” And as they went, they were cleansed of their leprosy.
17.15: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, came back to Jesus, shouting, “Praise God!”
17.16: He fell to the ground at Jesus’ feet, thanking him for what he had done. This man was a Samaritan.
17.17: Jesus asked, “Didn’t I heal ten men? Where are the other nine?
17.18: Has no one returned to give glory to God except this foreigner?”
17.19: And Jesus said to the man, “Stand up and go. Your faith has healed you.”
17.20: One day the Pharisees asked Jesus, “When will the Kingdom of God come?” Jesus replied, “The Kingdom of God can’t be detected by visible signs.
17.21: You won’t be able to say, ‘Here it is!’ or ‘It’s over there!’ For the Kingdom of God is already among you.”
17.22: Then he said to his disciples, “The time is coming when you will long to see the day when the Son of Man returns, but you won’t see it.
17.23: People will tell you, ‘Look, there is the Son of Man,’ or ‘Here he is,’ but don’t go out and follow them.
17.24: For as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so it will be on the day when the Son of Man comes.
17.25: But first the Son of Man must suffer terribly and be rejected by this generation.
17.26: “When the Son of Man returns, it will be like it was in Noah’s day.
17.27: In those days, the people enjoyed banquets and parties and weddings right up to the time Noah entered his boat and the flood came and destroyed them all.
17.28: “And the world will be as it was in the days of Lot. People went about their daily business—eating and drinking, buying and selling, farming and building—
17.29: until the morning Lot left Sodom. Then fire and burning sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.
17.30: Yes, it will be ‘business as usual’ right up to the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
17.31: On that day a person out on the deck of a roof must not go down into the house to pack. A person out in the field must not return home.
17.32: Remember what happened to Lot’s wife!
17.33: If you cling to your life, you will lose it, and if you let your life go, you will save it.
17.34: That night two people will be asleep in one bed; one will be taken, the other left.
17.35: Two women will be grinding flour together at the mill; one will be taken, the other left.”
17.37: “Where will this happen, Lord?” the disciples asked. Jesus replied, “Just as the gathering of vultures shows there is a carcass nearby, so these signs indicate that the end is near.”
17.36: Footnote: Some manuscripts add verse 36, Two men will be working in the field; one will be taken, the other left. Compare Matt 24:40.

7.1: When Jesus had finished saying all this to the people, he returned to Capernaum.
7.2: At that time the highly valued slave of a Roman officer was sick and near death.
7.3: When the officer heard about Jesus, he sent some respected Jewish elders to ask him to come and heal his slave.
7.4: So they earnestly begged Jesus to help the man. “If anyone deserves your help, he does,” they said,
7.5: “for he loves the Jewish people and even built a synagogue for us.”
7.6: So Jesus went with them. But just before they arrived at the house, the officer sent some friends to say, “Lord, don’t trouble yourself by coming to my home, for I am not worthy of such an honor.
7.7: I am not even worthy to come and meet you. Just say the word from where you are, and my servant will be healed.
7.8: I know this because I am under the authority of my superior officers, and I have authority over my soldiers. I only need to say, ‘Go,’ and they go, or ‘Come,’ and they come. And if I say to my slaves, ‘Do this,’ they do it.”
